newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDESPar to sell stakes in power firms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDESPar to sell stakes in power firms.

text.p: Brazil's BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar) said it plans to sell a 10 percent voting stake in Bahia state power distributor Coelba next week.
Moreover, the bank plans to sell a 0.5 percent voting stake in federal power utility Eletrobras in the second week of March, said Sergio Weguelin, BNDESPar's manager.

BNDESPar, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), will hold the sales on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange but it has not yet set a date for the auctions because it is still awaiting approval from Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM).
Weguelin said tender documents for both sales would be published 48 hours before the auction date.
BNDESPar is planning to sell 10 billion common shares of Coelba for a minimum price of 62 reais per 1,000 shares if the company's stock is traded below this price one day before the auction date.
If Coelba's shares surpass 62 reais, the minimum price will be the average price of the company's shares in the last 20 trading sessions, Weguelin said.
He said 15 financial institutions including ING Barings, Salomon Brothers/Patrimonio, Pactual and Bozano Simonsen had been chosen to coordinate the Coelba share sale.
Weguelin said BNDESPar would sell in the second week of March 400,000 Eletrobras's units made up of 400 million Eletrobras common shares and call options which will mature on Dec 15.
He said the minimum price for Eletrobras units would be equivalent to 104.83 percent the company's average common stock price on the day of the auction.
Pariba, Banco Omega, Citibank's brokerage and Bozano, Simonsen were among the 15 financial institutions selected to lead manage the sale, he said.
BNDESPar currently holds 19 percent of Eletrobras voting stock.
